items.alt: The demo board's enclosure in the enclosure designer: the tools down the left over the Features list (a cut-out and a hole in the front, vents in the left wall, DEMO on the top in orange); in the middle the box in 3D with its white top lifted off the charcoal base and the board inside, and under it the top drawn flat with the board's parts and the orange text; on the right the box's Properties with its size, weight, filament and colours.

items.text: The box: a base and a flat lid, or two shells joined part-way up the walls; corners rounded, top and bottom edges square, rounded or chamfered. It closes with a press fit, snap catches, or M2 to M4 screws (in bosses in the box's corners, or down through the board's mounting holes) into a pilot hole, a heat-set insert or a captive nut, countersunk or pan head, with the screw length they take. The board sits on standoffs at its mounting holes, or on ledges under its corners when it has none; posts from the top can hold it down.

Openings are found for the parts at the board's edge and for LEDs, switches and displays under the top; a part that reaches into a wall gets a slot open to the joint, so the board drops in. Add your own: holes (countersunk or counterbored for a screw), cut-outs, slots, pockets, vents (slots, holes or a honeycomb), bosses with a screw hole, pins, blocks and ribs (outside or inside any face), text, and logos from SVG drawings (cut in, raised or cut through). Duplicate, mirror, repeat in a row, centre or delete the feature you picked; undo and redo for every change to the box.

The face view draws a face flat as seen from outside, with the parts behind it. Zoom with the wheel, drag the background to pan; a grid and rulers in millimetres, and the picked feature's distances to the face's edges. Features are dragged into place, and openings, vents and protrusions sized by their handles; they snap to the middle across the face (on a wall, also to the board's top and halfway up the inside) and to the middles of the parts and other features (the line is shown), else to 0.5 mm (0.1 mm with Shift). Double-click a part to make its opening.

Also: recesses for stick-on feet, mounting ears, keyhole slots for hanging the box on a wall, light tubes down to LEDs, buttons onto switches printed as parts of their own, and a seal: a groove for a rubber cord, or a gasket printed in TPU.

Colours: each part's filament colour (15 common ones, or any other) and finish (matte, satin, gloss, silk, metal, clear or fuzzy skin), shown in 3D. Text and logos can have a colour of their own, for printing in two colours: raised, they stand out in it; cut in, the cut is filled flush with it.

Made for printing: set the nozzle, layer height, material and hole allowance. Round holes in walls become teardrops (unless you turn it off), vent bars and text strokes follow the nozzle, the edges on the bed get a small chamfer, and checks point out thin walls, long bridges, protrusions and parts that run into something, and shallow text. See the parts laid out as they print, or a section through the box. Export STL (one colour), 3MF (each part an object of its own in its colour, text in another colour a part of the object it prints with) or STEP (the box with the board in place, in their colours).

Export › Picture (PNG) saves a picture of the box to show, up to 8192 pixels a side (40 megapixels in all): in a room of any colour (its background shaded, flat or left see-through), lit by a key light from the direction and height you set and by the room's light all round, with a soft shadow under it; as the view shows it or from a side, with a preview.
items.alt: A picture made by Export › Picture (PNG): the demo board's box from above and in front, a charcoal base with a cut-out and a hole in the front showing the green board inside and vent slots in the side, a white top with DEMO in orange, on a light grey studio background with a soft shadow under it.

items.text: ActiveRoute routes each connection on one of the chosen layers, with no vias. Route Guide: draw the way the selected connections should go, and they are routed side by side along it, in the order they meet it, on alternate layers where their pads allow. Its width is worked out from the connections' tracks and gaps; Up and Down change it while you draw, and it shows how many connections fit. Track-Track Space in Route Guide widens the spacing between routes (never below their width and clearance rules); Tune Selected tunes the selected nets to their Matched Lengths rules.

Pin Swapping: with Pin Swap Routing on, ActiveRoute first swaps pins within their swap groups, on the selected components that have pin swapping on, where that shortens the connections. The PCB ActiveRoute panel lists the components that have pin swap groups and turns pin swapping on or off for each.

Design Rule Check: a polygon pour's own copper is no longer reported against a keep-out unless it lies over it, and a solid pour's copper is named Polygon Region in the messages; Silk To Solder Mask Clearance is measured from each pad's actual solder mask opening (or, checking clearance to exposed copper, from the copper that opening bares); and the messages are in the board's units (millimetres on a metric board). Polygon pours now flow round keep-out arcs, and solder mask Gerbers give a through pad its opening from its pad stack.
With display scaling (125 %, 150 % and so on), the multi-board assembly's 3D view now fits its panel, so a click picks what is under the pointer.

releases.title: Diagrams

items.text: Diagrams: a new document type (.DgmDoc) for block diagrams, flowcharts and circuit sketches beside your design. File › New › Diagram makes one; so do the Home page and Add New to Project › Other. A block can be linked to one of the project's schematic sheets (Ctrl+click it to open the sheet), and Add Project Sheets draws the project's sheet hierarchy as linked blocks.
items.alt: A diagram in the demo project: the Shapes panel with its Electrical library open, the project's sheets as blocks linked to them (Demo picked, its Format panel showing its colours and its linked sheet), a battery joined to the Demo block, a diode and an LED from the library, and a yellow note with a formatted label.

items.text: The Shapes panel: General, Misc, Advanced and Electrical libraries (37 circuit symbols drawn for Konium Designer, from resistors and transistors to logic gates), and the project's schematic sheets; search by name. Click a shape to add it beside the selected one, joined to it, or drag it onto the page; hovering shows it larger.

Drawing: shapes moved, resized, turned (in 15° steps, or freely with Alt) and flipped, with guides to line them up. Hover arrows add a joined copy or start a connector. Connectors end on a shape's outline or on one of its connection points and go straight, orthogonal, simple, isometric, curved or entity-relation. Straight, curved and isometric ones have waypoints to drag, add and remove; orthogonal and simple ones have segments to drag. Connectors can jump where they cross, and have 24 kinds of line end.

The Format panel: the page's grid, page view, paper size and background; a shape's quick styles, fill, gradient, line, shadow, opacity and rounding; its text's font, size, bold, italic, underline, alignment, position, colours and spacing; its size, position, angle, order, grouping, alignment and spacing out. Edit Style, Copy and Paste Style, Set as Default Style. Labels can be formatted as you type them (bold, italic, colours, sizes, lists), with a formatting bar.

Pages, layers (shown or hidden, locked, renamed, shapes moved between them), groups, containers that take in what is dropped on them, lists that stack their items, copy, cut, paste and duplicate, lock, find, undo and redo. While a diagram is in front the menu bar has Edit, Arrange and Extras, and View has the diagram's own items. Edit Data keeps a shape's properties, Edit Link a web address or another page (Ctrl+click follows it), Edit Diagram shows a page's XML. The toolbar's Insert › Image (or a picture dropped on the page) puts a picture in.

Export a page, or what is selected, as PNG, SVG or PDF (made by the print dialog's Save as PDF), and print the current page on the diagram's paper (in page view, sheet by sheet). Diagrams from other tools: .drawio files and Visio drawings (.vsdx) open as Konium Designer diagrams, by File › Open or the Import Wizard (a Visio drawing's pages, shapes, groups, connectors, text, fill and line), and Extras › Export as saves a diagram as a .drawio file or a Visio drawing (.vsdx).

File › New › Multi-board Schematic and Multi-board Assembly are now also in the File menu when no document is open, or when the document in front has no editor of its own (a BOM document, an output job).

releases.title: Digi-Key and Mouser in the BOM

items.text: BOM documents: a line's part can now also be searched for at Digi-Key and at Mouser, chosen beside the Solutions panel's search box, besides the public copy of JLCPCB's parts list. These searches go through Konium's parts service at konium.app, which holds Konium's own keys for them; only what is typed in the search box is sent. A result shows the distributor's part number, the manufacturer's part number, the packaging, the minimum order where it is more than one, stock and the price for the run's quantity, and can be added to the line as a part choice with its price breaks.

The parts service keeps each search's answer for a day and gives it again without asking the distributor. Each user can make 100 new searches a day, and the service stays under Digi-Key's and Mouser's own daily and per-minute limits. Prices are shown in the currency the distributor gives them in: Digi-Key's in pounds, from its UK site.
Update Supplier Data now also looks Digi-Key and Mouser part choices up again by their own part numbers, for stock, prices and lifecycle status.
A BOM's cost is now added up separately for each currency, for example pounds and dollars. Before, prices in different currencies were added together.

Network Activity lists the Digi-Key and Mouser searches and where they go. Answers from Konium's own services (AI and parts) are no longer kept by the offline copy, so the AI allowance shown is read afresh each time.

releases.title: BOM tools, rules from the schematic, and the previously greyed options finished

items.text: BOM part choices and cost: a line of a BOM document can now be given part choices. A line has one without any action only when the BOM document already holds choices for it (shown and priced as saved, whatever the supplier), or when its part's parameters carry an LCSC number, a manufacturer part number or a supplier part number (a choice with no price until it is looked up). Any other line needs one added, by hand or by searching a public copy of JLCPCB's parts list (jlcsearch.tscircuit.com) one line at a time, by LCSC number, part number or value and package; a result shows stock, price breaks and Basic or Extended where the list gives them. With a production quantity set, the cost per board and for the run is worked out from the lines that have prices. BOM Checks flag a line with no part, a part with no supplier, too little stock where the stock is known, a saved part choice with no price, a risky lifecycle, parts in one line that differ in a parameter, and repeated designators or line numbers. Update Supplier Data looks the LCSC part numbers up again for stock and prices, and Export For JLCPCB saves the BOM with the columns of JLCPCB's assembly BOM (Comment, Designator, Footprint, LCSC Part #).
items.alt: The demo project's BOM document grouped by comment and footprint, for a production quantity of 100: five lines given parts found by LCSC number in the public copy of JLCPCB's parts list, with their unit prices and subtotals, the cost per board and for the run from the five priced lines, BOM Checks flagging the connector with no part, and the resistor's part choice with its price and description.

items.text: Fill Part Numbers With AI asks the AI model for a manufacturer part for each BOM line with no part choice (or for every line, if chosen). Each suggestion is looked up in the same copy of JLCPCB's parts list before it is offered, and you tick the ones to keep. It runs on the Konium AI service, your own key, or a model on your computer or network.

The Konium AI service's daily allowance is now 25 job tokens. A job takes one on the cheapest model offered, and on a dearer model about as many as it costs times more. Preferences › System › AI shows each model's tokens a job, and a job's cost line shows what it takes and how many are left today.

Rules from the schematic: Add as Rule on a Parameter Set or a component carries design rules (width, clearance, via style, masks, hole sizes, impedance and more). Update PCB Document adds them to the board, scoped to the net the Parameter Set sits on, or to the component. In Design › Rules, the Rule Wizard... button adds its rule to the rules being edited.
items.alt: The Engineering Change Order from the demo schematic: besides the components, net and pins to add, an Add Rules group with a Width rule scoped to InNet('VIN'), from a Parameter Set placed on the VIN wire.

items.text: Compiled sheets: after a compile, tabs under a sheet show it as compiled, or one tab per channel of a repeated sheet, with each instance's designators, net labels, ports, sheet entries, power ports, and document and sheet numbers. Compiled views are read-only; the Editor tab goes back to editing.

Schematic and libraries: a component's Library Name can be unticked, so the part is looked for in any library, and its Table Name, so a database part is looked for in any of the library's tables; the IBIS and Signal Integrity entries under its models' Add... open Model Assignments. Browse Libraries' Find... searches every library by name or description, and its 3D button shows a footprint in 3D (the PCB Model dialog too). Place Component can place a schematic library's part, its footprint, designator and comment taken from it. Where libraries are looked for can be set: open ones, the project's and Installed Libraries; the project's and open ones only; or Installed Libraries only.

Show Differences: Advanced Mode compares one schematic with the board. OrCAD designs: a part's footprint can come from a Part Field on import, and Orcad ports mode sizes a port to its name and places it with one click.

Library options: the PCB library's Snap To Grids and a sheet round the footprint; the schematic library's Style (Standard or ANSI), kept in the library file. The PCB library's Component Rule Check adds Shorted Copper (copper joining pads of different names) and Unconnected Copper (copper that reaches no pad or via).

Board Insight: the net under the cursor lights up as it passes over (Live Highlighting, fading in and out over the times set, or only with Shift held). The heads-up display (Shift+H) shows beside the cursor where it is, how far from the last click (Insert or a click makes a new delta origin), the current layer and the snap grid; rest the cursor a moment and it adds what lies under it: a summary, the component, and up to three of the nets, objects and violations. Pad and via names are drawn in the font and sizes chosen, dark or light against the pad, and Monochrome Other Layers can join Shift+S.
items.alt: The demo board with the heads-up display beside the cursor over C1's first pad: its position and its distance from the origin, the layer and snap grid, then the four objects under it (a pad, two tracks and a 3D body), their nets VIN and GND, the component C1, and the pad and tracks one by one; the VIN net lit up by live highlighting.

items.text: Board display: a net's colour override drawn checkered, striped or solid over its layer colour, and as set when zoomed out; objects in violation hatched, cross-hatched or solid; locked objects textured; selected objects outlined unless Highlight In Full; tiny strings drawn as boxes and hairline tracks as single lines (Draft Thresholds); hard-edged text; the selection area shaded; masked objects see-through or solid; the DRC overlay and its crosses each with its own switch.

View Configurations: every kind of object drawn Final, Draft (as outlines) or Hidden, Coordinates and Rooms included; the System Colours rows, among them DRC markers, the large grid, highlighting, the board's and the sheet's lines, a workspace gradient and Measure Distance's lines; with Display Sheet on, the sheet drawn under the board. Mechanical layers can stay in view in single layer mode, or be linked to the sheet: shown only with it and, with Lock sheet primitives on, out of reach. In 3D, Show Rooms draws rooms as see-through boxes. View Options: special strings converted, connection lines in their ends' layer colours, component reference points, testpoint marks, the object under the cursor in the status bar, planes filled in their nets' colours, and a colour for new nets.

Board Options: Snap To Grids, Linear and Point Guides, Object Axis (placing lines up with nearby pads, vias and track ends, a guide line drawn) and Arc Centres, with the Axis Snap Range, kept in the board file. Grids... and Guides... open the Grid and Guide Managers, and Auto-size to linked layers fits the sheet round them. Route Tool Path names the router's layer: in 3D a one-piece board is milled along it.
Layer Stack Manager: Presets (two to twelve layers), Save and Load a stack as a file, and a 3D option that draws each layer as a slab beside its row.
items.alt: The Layer Stack Manager with the Six Layer preset: each layer drawn in 3D beside its row, from the overlays and solder masks through the signal layers, internal planes, cores and prepregs, with thicknesses, materials and dielectric constants.

items.text: PCB editing: a click on overlapping objects lists them to choose from, and Shift Click To Select keeps the kinds you tick from a plain click. Smart Component Snap, Snap To Room Hot Spots, Protect Locked Objects, Click Clears Selection, Double Click Runs Inspector, Comp Drag, and Undo/Redo setting how many steps are kept (30 by default, 0 for no limit). A partly routed net's connection lines run from where its copper ends (Smart Track Ends). A component moved onto others can stop short of them (Avoid) or push them aside (Push). Autopan can re-centre, jump or glide at a set speed. Paste takes a drawing (SVG) or text another application copied, when nothing from a board is on Konium Designer's clipboard.

Pads and routing: Pad Template takes the size, shape and hole of another of the board's pads, named by shape, size and hole (such as c150h100); Electrical Type; Edit Full Pad Layer Definition, for a through pad that has a per-layer stack; the bottom solder mask expansion unlinked from the top, and a through pad's or a via's opening measured from the hole's edge (Gerber output follows both); the Assembly testpoint ticks. Interactive Routing: with User Choice widths and Apply to all layers off, a layer keeps a width of its own while the board is open, and Template picks one of the board's via sizes. Re-Annotate names each component from where it is (Name from Position), and Fanout can lead each via out from under its component (escape routes).
Preferences › PCB Editor › Defaults: Component, Coordinate, Dimension and Polygon can be edited; the next one placed starts from them, and Save As / Load carry them with the rest.

Boards carry their fonts: TrueType fonts embedded in a board draw its strings, and with Embed TrueType fonts on, saving a binary board puts in it the fonts its strings use, once the browser (Chrome or Edge) is allowed to read this computer's fonts. A substitution font is drawn for text whose font this computer doesn't have. The File Format Change Report says what may differ in a board saved by another version of the format. Remove Duplicates leaves exact duplicates out of Gerber and NC drill files and the files output jobs write, and Confirm Global Edit asks before a PCB List change goes to every selected object.

Outputs: PCB reports (Netlist Status, Board Information, a BGA's fanout, Move Component Origin To Grid, Stackup Compatibility) can be shown, written as text or HTML to the project's outputs folder, or both. DRC Sub-Net Details lists an un-routed net's pieces. Gerber: Include unconnected mid-layer pads, off by default, so inner-layer pads that connect to nothing are now left out unless it is ticked; with Embedded apertures off, RS-274-D files sharing one aperture list (.APR), which the CAM document opened after generating reads them with. NC Drill: Optimise change location commands (on by default, so a coordinate that hasn't changed is left out), slots routed by default or drilled with G85, and Generate Board Edge Rout Paths with the Rout Tool Dia given; output jobs keep them all. Impedance formulas: Helper puts in variables, functions and operators.

The desktop: Reopen Last Workspace and Restore open documents; a panel layout for each kind of document; the documents bar putting a kind's tabs under one when they don't all fit, wrapping onto several lines, or hiding while only one document is open; with Dynamic transparency on, floating panels growing see-through as the cursor nears while a tool is at work; a Clipboard panel; Document Path; the startup screen, popup panel delays and shadows round menus and panels; the window's title naming the document; document tabs of equal width; middle click closes a tab.

Navigation: cross-probing can dim everything else, or draw the net as a connection graph; Zooming, Masking, Selecting and Include Power Parts decide what it does. The Navigator lists a net's pins, net labels, ports, sheet entries, sheet connectors and, if asked, its wires; Cross Select Mode can instead zoom to the matching objects when their document is next shown, or mask the rest.

Projects panel: documents grouped by class, by type or not at all; open and modified status; each document's number in the project; the sheet structure or a plain list; sorting; a schematic's sheet symbols and ports under it; each document's path from the project folder in its tooltip; and what a single click does. Two defaults change: only Source Documents start open, and a single click brings an open document to the front (a closed one opens with a double-click). Both can be set back.

Data management: File › New › Schematic can start from a sheet template chosen once; auto save can also copy to a folder you choose (Chrome or Edge), while the browser allows it; Tab's changes to power ports, net labels, off sheet connectors, junctions, No ERC markers, bus entries and text are kept between sessions unless Permanent is on; Temporary Mesh Data shows how many 3D models are kept and can clear them; Show VCS status gives each document's number of versions in Local History; Use localised resources writes dates, times and counts as your computer's language does; the text editor's Insert key can switch to overwriting.
Every option in Preferences and in the editors' dialogs that was greyed out as not yet built now works. The planned features are still greyed, labelled as planned.

releases.title: Signal Integrity, multi-board and harness design

items.text: Signal Integrity: Tools › Signal Integrity (schematic and PCB) screens every net, with drivers and receivers by the schematic's pin types, IC models by technology (CMOS-3.3V, CMOS-5V, CMOS-2.5V, CMOS-1.8V, LVTTL, TTL) or IBIS (Model Assignments › Import IBIS), the copper as transmission lines from the layer stack, input capacitance, clamps, series parts and parts to the rails, and lists each net's status with the overshoot and undershoot of each edge; Show Columns adds the top and base values, flight times, slopes, length and impedance. The picked net shows its pins and the terminations to try, each with its value worked out from the line.
items.alt: The Signal Integrity panel under the demo board with two long lines added: each net's status and overshoot, CLK's driver and receiver, and the terminations with their suggested values, the series resistor ticked

items.text: Reflections... draws the picked nets' waveforms in SimView, driven by the stimulus (a single pulse, a constant level or pulses), unterminated and with each termination ticked; Crosstalk... the noise an aggressor puts on the near and far ends of the nets beside it. Setup Options (track impedance and length for the schematic alone, the default technology, supply nets, the stimulus), Set Tolerances and the panel's terminations are kept in the project.
items.alt: SimView with CLK's reflections: the driver's and the receiver's waveforms ringing unterminated, and calm with a series resistor

items.text: Signal Integrity rules: Signal Stimulus, Overshoot and Undershoot of each edge, Impedance, Signal Top and Base Value, Flight Time and Slope of each edge and Supply Nets are in Design › Rules with their constraints, and Design Rule Check checks them when they are ticked in its Rules To Check: each net a rule takes simulated and held to it.

Multi-board design: multi-board projects (.PrjMbd) open with their child projects. The multi-board schematic (.MbsDoc) shows the modules, their entries and the direct, wire, cable and harness connections between them; Place Module, Import From Child Projects (connectors by their System = Connector parameter, with their pins and nets) and moving modules edit it, and the side lists every pin the boards share (pin to pin, with the net on each board) and what doesn't meet. The multi-board assembly (.MbaDoc) shows the boards in 3D where the assembly puts them, with mechanical parts from their STEP models; pick a board to move or turn it, Insert Board adds one. Both are saved in their own format, the rest of each file untouched.

Harness design: harness projects (.PrjHar) open with their wiring diagram in front. Wiring diagrams (.WirDoc) and layout drawings (.LdrDoc) open as sheets: connectors with their pins, wires, splices, cables, shields and twists; the layout's bundles and connection points: moved and edited as on a schematic, saved with everything kept. Reports › Harness Wire List gives each wire's ends, colour, cable, shield and twist, and its length along the layout's bundles; save it as CSV. Harness Draftsman drawings (.HarDwf) open as Draftsman documents.

Network activity (the Home page, and Preferences › System › Network Activity): Allow network activity: off, Konium Designer makes no connections at all (no updates, What's New, AI jobs, supplier data or reports), and the browser itself is told to refuse any the page could make, so it holds whatever the code does; Offline shows beside the menus while it is off. Check konium.app for updates and What's New: off, Konium Designer doesn't ask, and a copy installed from konium.app stays on the version it has. Network Activity and Help › About list every connection Konium Designer makes: when, where to, what goes, and whether it is allowed. The website's visit count runs only at konium.app itself, never in a downloaded copy.

Help › Contact the Author: a message to Konium Designer's author (a question, a comment, or a request to audit Konium Designer's source code), sent through konium.app, which keeps the author's address (it isn't in Konium Designer). About now says how Konium Designer is made: from scratch, by its author, with the help of AI tools.

What's New gives each release's SHA-256 checksum at the right of its heading, from this one on: the checksum of its single file as a download saves it (Konium-26.099.html for this one), to check a copy is the one published (Windows: certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256; macOS and Linux: shasum -a 256 <file>). Click it to copy it.

The Konium AI service's daily allowance is now counted in jobs on the cheapest model it offers: a dearer model's job uses as many as it costs times more, so the day's allowance costs about the same whichever model is chosen. Each model's share is beside it in Preferences › System › AI, and each job's cost line says how much it takes.

releases.title: Design Adviser, Draftsman drawings and ActiveBOM documents

items.text: Design Adviser: Tools › Design Adviser opens the Design Adviser panel. Check Design has the model you choose review the project (or the sheet in front) before layout, as an experienced engineer would: supplies and decoupling, floating inputs and enable pins, missing pull-ups, UART, I2C, SPI, USB and CAN wired the wrong way, regulators', crystals' and LEDs' parts, nets that look alike but aren't joined. Only the design as text goes (parts, pins, nets), and the panel says what goes where and what it costs first. Each finding has its severity, why, the fix, and its parts and nets, shown on the sheet at a click; dismissed findings stay dismissed; Copy puts the review on the clipboard.

In depth: each part worth it (ICs, transistors, crystals, regulators, connectors with a part number) is checked against its own datasheet (a PDF you add or drop on the panel, the link in its parameters, else one the model finds on the web), pin by pin: what each pin is joined to, the parts the datasheet asks for and their values, the rails against its ratings, the symbol against the pin table. Findings give the datasheet pages they rest on (a click shows the page). Ask: questions about the design and the review, answered with the design, the datasheets and the review in view.

On the board: with a PCB in front the adviser checks it before it is made: its layers and rules, each component's place and side, each IC supply pad's nearest capacitors and how far they are, crystals' distances, each net's length, widths, vias and pours, unrouted connections, differential pairs, parts by the edge, exposed pads' vias: all measured in Konium Designer and sent as text with the schematic and what the datasheets said about layout. Findings are selected on the board at a click.
items.alt: The Design Adviser panel beside the demo board: what it sends, the board's review with a warning about C2's distance from U1's output, and the parts and nets shown on the board

items.text: Draftsman documents: .PCBDwf files open in their own tab. Each sheet is drawn with its border and zones and its board assembly and fabrication views from the project's board at their scale, side and rotation (the board outline stored in the drawing when the board isn't open), drill tables, bills of materials, layer stack tables, text and title blocks; items not drawn yet show as named boxes and are kept. Drag an item to move it, change its scale, side, rotation, title or text on the right, delete it, add, remove or resize sheets, undo and redo, print every sheet, and save it back in its own format, the rest of the file untouched. File › New › Draftsman Document lays a new one out for the board: assembly and fabrication views, drill, layer stack and BOM tables, notes and a title block.
items.alt: A new Draftsman document for the demo board: top and bottom assembly views, the fabrication view, the drill, layer stack and BOM tables, and the top view's properties

items.text: BOM documents are now ActiveBOM files (.BomDoc), read and written in their own format (the columns shown and their widths, sorting, grouping, not-fitted parts, line numbering and each line's part choices, the rest of the file untouched), with lines made as ActiveBOM makes them. Set Line Numbers numbers the lines from the document's start and step; Export saves the BOM as Excel, CSV, tab-delimited text or a web page.

Design Rule Check › Creepage Distance is measured round cutouts, slots and unplated holes: the shortest way across the board's surface that keeps out of them. Before, a pair with one of them between it wasn't reported, even where the copper beside it was too near.
Interactive Routing at any angle (forum): Shift+Space reaches any angle while routing tracks, as on lines: Preferences › PCB Editor › Interactive Routing › Restrict To 90/45 is off by default.

Coming next: Signal Integrity, multi-board and harness design, BOM supply and cost with JLCPCB stock and prices, diagrams, ActiveRoute's Route Guide and Pin Swapping, and an enclosure designer are already in the menus, greyed as planned features: each is switched on in a release of its own.

releases.title: Component Builder: schematic symbols from pin tables

items.text: Tools › Component Builder makes schematic symbols too: Create Symbol (a variant's Symbol tab or column, or Create Symbols for the ticked variants) reads the variant's pin table (its pages' text, and pictures of them) and lays the pins round a body on a 100 mil grid: supplies on top, grounds below, inputs left, outputs right, the other pins by function group, each group together; a connector's in number order, a diode's anodes facing its cathodes, a transistor's gate or base left. Active-low names get AD's overbar. Variants with the same pinout share one reading.
items.alt: The Component Builder's Symbol tab for a made-up USB-to-UART bridge in QFN-24: the symbol drawn with its pins grouped, the checks against the footprint, and the pin table to edit

items.text: The symbol's review: every pin to change (number, name, active low, type, side), Sides by Function or by Number, the symbol drawn as it will be, and checks against the variant's footprint: pins without a pad, pads without a pin, numbers used twice, a pin count that doesn't match the package. Add to Library puts it in an open schematic library or a new one, linked to its footprint.
Preferences › Schematic › Default Primitives › Pin › Length: Place › Pin and the builder's symbols start with it (AD's 300mil).
Also: the model lists run from the cheapest (Gemini Flash, the default) to the dearest; the model can't be changed while a job is under way; the builder's fields, buttons and reviews line up.

releases.title: Component Builder: footprints from datasheets; track corners with arcs; AD's layer drawing order

items.text: Tools › Component Builder (in a schematic or PCB library): a datasheet PDF read in Konium Designer, then surveyed by an AI model: every orderable variant, its part numbers, package, pins, lead form, body, pitch and pinout, and the pages of its drawing, land pattern and pin table; the part number you will use ticks its own variant, and any page is shown at a click. Then Create Footprint: the variant's drawings found on their pages and read enlarged: the package family by the drawing's shape, its dimensions, and the datasheet's own land pattern (rows, staggered rows, shield slots, unplated posts, the outline), or the footprint worked out by IPC-7351B from the dimensions when the datasheet draws none (DIP by IPC-7251). Each step shows as it goes, with its time.
items.alt: The Component Builder on a USB-C receptacle's datasheet: the variant surveyed, its land pattern read, measured on the drawing and checked, the footprint beside the datasheet's page

items.text: The pads are measured in the drawing itself: the model says which pads there are, their names and sizes; their places come from the drawing, on the lines the PDF draws (each pad's exact edges), so a stagger between rows or a row's distance comes out as drawn. Then the footprint is drawn and shown back to the model with the datasheet's drawing, its pads outlined in red over it, and the model puts right what doesn't match until it finds nothing more (Preferences › System › AI › Footprint checks: up to 3 rounds). A drawing not to scale is said so.

The review beside the datasheet's page: the dimensions and pads to edit, Add Pad, Mirror and Rotate, checks (pin count, pitch, overlapping pads, unconverted inches, what the model's check found), the footprint drawn as it will be; then Add to Library (the open PCB library or a new one) with courtyard, silkscreen, assembly outline, 3D body and pin-1 mark. What you accept from a public datasheet can be shared, so the next person reading it gets it at once.

Preferences › System › AI, off until switched on: the Konium service (free within a daily allowance), your own key (OpenRouter, or any endpoint that speaks OpenAI's chat completions; the key stays in this browser), or a model on your computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). One model does every job, chosen there or in the builder: the latest Claude Opus, GPT Sol, Gemini Pro or Gemini Flash (the default), each always its family's newest. Before anything is sent the builder says what goes where and what it costs; nothing leaves the computer unless you start a job.

Land-pattern drawings made up with their answers (rows, quad packages, chips, SOT, headers, connectors with staggered rows and shield slots, flex connectors, ball grids, drawn every way datasheets draw them) measure Konium Designer's measuring and the models, and are the start of a footprint model of Konium Designer's own.
items.alt: Four made-up land-pattern drawings: a staggered connector with shield slots, a QFN, a ball grid and a flex connector, dimensioned as datasheets dimension them

items.text: Track corners as AD (forum): Shift+Space cycles 45°, 45° with arc, 90°, 90° with arc and any angle in Interactive Routing and Place Track / Line; in the arc modes , and . shrink and grow the arc (Shift faster), smaller where the clearance needs.

Layers drawn in AD's Layer Drawing Order (forum: the silkscreen was hidden under the mechanical layers): multi-layer pads and vias, the overlays, the connection lines, the current layer, the other signal layers, paste, solder mask, planes, drill guide, keep-out, mechanical layers, drill drawing, the grid; the grid now shows on the board. Preferences › PCB Editor › Display › Layer Drawing Order changes it (Promote, Demote, Default); with the board flipped the bottom side's layers come over the top's.
items.alt: Preferences › PCB Editor › Display with the Layer Drawing Order dialog: Multi Layer, Top Overlay, Bottom Overlay … Visible Grids

items.text: Sharper drawing: System › View › Smooth edges off draws lines, edges and fills hard on whole screen pixels; on smooths filled shapes too. On displays scaled to 125 % or 150 % the drawing is made at the screen's own pixels, not stretched.

Units as the document has them: a board opens in its Board Options unit and each document keeps its own (Q changes the active one's); a schematic's dialogs and panels use the sheet's unit, as AD does; a length typed with its unit (2.54mm, 100mil) is taken as written.

Also: Ctrl + drag on a selected polygon's edge adds a vertex there; View Configurations' T, B, E, R and 1, 2, 3 … switch layers on and off as in AD; Preferences opens at the page last open; the IPC wizard makes SOJ packages, and a lopsided package's courtyard (DPAK, SOT-223) follows its pads and body.

releases.title: Design Rule Check as AD's, every rule kind; ActiveRoute; fab-house profiles

items.text: Design Rule Check follows the board's own Rules To Check (Online and Batch, kept in the board as AD keeps them), its Report Options and its stop count, with AD's defaults for a board without them. Violations a designer waived in AD are left out and listed in the report with their comment, author and date. One violation per pair of objects; objects described on their own layers.
items.alt: The showcase board with the Design Rule Checker's Report Options: shorting copper, broken planes, dead copper, starved thermals

items.text: Every AD rule kind but Signal Integrity is checked now. New: Modified Polygon, Height, Un-Connected Pin, Net Antennae, Acute Angle, Length and Matched Lengths (in length or in delay), SMD Neck-Down, SMD To Corner, SMD To Plane, SMD Entry, Vias Under SMD, Routing Via Style, Routing Layers, Differential Pairs Routing (widths, uncoupled length), Parallel Segment, Daisy Chain Stub Length, Maximum Via Count, Max Via Stub Length (Back Drilling), Return Path, Creepage Distance, Minimum Solder Mask Sliver, Silk To Solder Mask, Silk To Silk, Silk To Board Region, Component Clearance (3D bodies), Permitted Layers, Layer Pairs, Fabrication and Assembly Testpoint Style and Usage. The Report Options too: drilled SMT pads, multilayer pads with no hole, net ties' shorting copper, broken planes, dead copper and starved thermals, as warnings.
items.alt: Rules To Check › High Speed: Parallel Segment to Return Path, each ticked for Online and Batch as the board keeps it

items.text: Fewer false violations: rule scopes asked as AD asks them (OnLayer, InPolygon, missing classes, No Net copper), Width limits per layer, net ties, keep-out restrictions, pad and via shapes per layer, Different / Same Differential Pairs clearances, shelved polygons, regions to their arc resolution, board outline arcs to 0.005 mil, copper text by its strokes. Every region was taken twice (AD keeps each in two streams): now once. Split planes inside split planes take their own area. Checked against AD's own waivers on public boards and against a bug report's board that AD passes with no violations: none found there either. A large board's clearance check 59 s → 11 s.

Route › ActiveRoute (Shift+A) and the PCB ActiveRoute panel: the selected components', pads' or routing's connections routed on the layers ticked in the panel, through vias; Meander tunes the routed nets up to their Matched Lengths rule's longest net, in the same undo step.

Design › Fab-House Profile…: JLCPCB, PCBWay, OSH Park, Eurocircuits and Aisler standard services (their own published capabilities, with the page and the date read) against the board's rules, those allowing less than the house makes in red. Check Board runs a Design Rule Check with the house's limits; Apply raises the general rules to them in one undo step.
items.alt: Design › Fab-House Profile on the showcase board: JLCPCB's limits against its rules, the hole size and mask sliver rules below them in red

items.text: Bug reports sent from Report a Bug can also be filed for the AI assistant that helps build Konium Designer, so a report reaches a fix sooner; the dialog says so.

Fixed: the Rules editor's constraints for Creepage, Return Path, Back Drilling and the testpoint styles, and AD's defaults for new rules of them; Silk To Solder Mask Clearance's value (the rules editor and CAMtastic's design check read another key); new boards' silk rule keeps silk off pads only, as AD's; the Fabrication Testpoint and Daisy Chain Stub Length rules named as AD names them.

releases.title: The CAM editor edits, checks and panelises; EDIF schematics; 3D modelling

items.text: The CAM editor edits: place flashes, lines, polylines, rectangles, polygons and voids, arcs and circles five ways each, text and dimensions; drills, slots, drilled text and routed circles. Cut, copy and paste, move, rotate, mirror, array, scale, break, chamfer, fillet, extend, join and offset; change D-codes, polarity and layers; composite layers and step-and-repeat blocks; selection by window, crossing, trace and filter; views such as negative, translucent and difference. Every CAMtastic command now works.

Netlist extraction (copper joined through plated holes, planes by their clearances and thermals) and comparison with an IPC-D-356 netlist; PCB Design Check (clearance, track width, annular rings, hole sizes, holes to copper, silk over pads, the rules taken from the open board); RFQ, D-code usage, DRC/DFM, rout, XY and netlist reports.
items.alt: The showcase board's films in the CAM editor: the design checked, the PCB RFQ Report over it

items.text: Panelise, film placement, copper pour, teardrops, venting, trim silkscreen, pad removal, homebase pads, epoxy bars and rout paths. Import and export ODB++, IPC-D-356, DXF and mill files; import HPGL and aperture lists; export centroids, bitmaps, and a board (.PcbDoc) made from the films. Macros record commands, clicks and answers and play them back.
items.alt: Tools › Panelize PCB: four of the showcase board in a framed panel

items.text: File › Export › EDIF Schematic (and the Export Wizard): the schematics as one EDIF 2 0 0 file: the symbols placed, power symbols and each schematic library as libraries, a page for each sheet with its parts, wires, labels, power ports and ports, every net by the name the project compiles it to.

3D model editor: Split an assembly (or several bodies in one model) into a part for each solid, placed as the assembly places it. Box corners and cylinder rims filleted or chamfered; Cone and Dome: all exact B-rep.
items.alt: The showcase board's STEP model split into its parts in the 3D model editor

items.text: Library editor › Place › Pin: after each pin the cursor steps one grid on (down the side, or along the row for pins pointing up or down) and the number counts up; click again without moving the mouse, or press Enter, to place the next.

Fixed: round rectangles with a corner radius larger than half the box draw as AD draws them; colours a file leaves out are black, as in AD; No ERC marks show their style (Thin Cross, Thick Cross, Small Cross, Checkbox, Triangle) and orientation; the EDIF import labels fewer nets.

releases.title: Auto Save and recovery, Local History, Storage Manager

items.text: Storage Manager (View › Workspace Panels › System): the project's files and each one's history: open a version, label it, revert to it (the file written as it was, the one it replaces kept), delete versions, purge the history, show the auto-saved copies.
items.alt: The Storage Manager beside the showcase's MCU sheet: its project files, and the sheet's Local History with a labelled version

items.text: Local History: each save keeps the file it replaces: in a History folder beside the project, zipped as AD does (Name.~(n).Ext.Zip), or in the browser for documents without a project folder. Preferences › Data Management › Local History sets the days kept.

Auto Save (Preferences › Data Management › Backup, on every 10 minutes): changed documents are copied into the browser, also when the page is hidden or closed. After a crash or a tab closed with work unsaved, the Home page offers them back (Open or Discard).
Updating: the app's page is asked for afresh whenever you're online, so a new version shows as soon as it's out (Update now waits for it to arrive).

releases.title: Rigid-flex coverlay and Advanced Rigid-Flex, EDIF, faster on large boards

items.text: Rigid-flex coverlay as a layer of its own: Layer Stack Manager › right-click a layer › Insert layer above or below › Coverlay, in the flex stacks, with its Coverlay Expansion. A flex region on such a stack is covered by it, or, with Custom Coverlays, by the polygons drawn for it (Design › Place Coverlay Polygon and Place Coverlay Cutout; Coverlay Actions). Openings for pads and vias as the solder mask's. The coverlay shows in Board Planning Mode and in 3D, and Gerber output writes a file for each coverlay layer (Gerber X2 too).
items.alt: The showcase's sensor head folded in 3D, its flex tail under the Top Coverlay

items.text: Advanced Rigid-Flex (Layer Stack Manager › Advanced › Rigid-Flex): regions stand on their own, with no split lines: Place › Board Region, Design › Slice Board Region, a region's corners dragged, Delete; the Board Region dialog's Priority decides which region shows where they overlap. Back to Standard when the regions meet edge to edge.
items.alt: The Layer Stack Manager on the showcase flex board: the Flex stack with its Top Coverlay, and the Rigid-Flex mode

items.text: EDIF 2 0 0 files open (Import Wizard › EDIF Files, File › Open, drops): schematic pages as sheets with the SchLib of their cells, parts turned and mirrored as drawn, nets with their names; a netlist with no drawings as parts in rows with their nets named. EAGLE 8 and later's modules: each instance's sheets under a sheet symbol for it, its parts named as on the board.

The netlist and model editor complete: Replace, Find Next Selected, Clear Browser Marks, Indent and Unindent, Change Case, Word Wrap, Code Templates, editor settings from Visual Studio, split views, and Preferences › Text Editors. SimView: a wave picked by its name dims the others (Wave › Clear Filter), waves cut, pasted and inserted, and more plots than fit scroll.
Large boards: Design Rule Check and Gerber output many times faster, polygon pours faster, and pours not triangulated again on every redraw.

Fixed: a keepout track stays one when its width or its union is changed; tracks routed on a board take nothing of its first track (locked, keepout, in a pour); a component exploded keeps its designator's font. Simulation: a library's .lib section is the only one read, an included file's .END no longer ends the netlist, a DC sweep that fails leaves its source as it was, a .TRAN starting past its stop is reported; wave expressions keep numbers apart from nodes named as numbers; model files are saved in the encoding they were read in. The text editor's Replace All replaces every match (past 10,000), and Indent works on a first empty line. SimView's cursor B reads its own wave; a chart's zoom and cursors stay with it when another is deleted. EAGLE sheets leave room for AD's title block.

releases.title: Simulation, the CAM editor, EAGLE and database libraries

items.text: Mixed-signal simulation: Design › Simulate › Mixed Sim runs the project's schematics in Konium Designer's own SPICE simulator, in the browser. Analyses Setup as AD lays it out: Operating Point, Transient with Fourier, DC Sweep, AC Small Signal, Transfer Function, Noise, Pole-Zero, Temperature and Parameter Sweeps, Monte Carlo. The results open in SimView: stacked plots, waves that are expressions of signals, cursors and their measurements, FFT, more Y axes, each sweep's runs drawn together. A part's SIM model is added or edited in the Sim Model dialog; netlists and models open in a text editor; Home has a simulation demo.
items.alt: SimView: the simulation demo's amplifier with R1 swept, the runs of each signal drawn together

items.text: The CAM editor: Gerber (RS-274X and X2) and NC drill files open as a CAM document, a layer per file, typed, coloured and stacked as AD's CAMtastic does them. The CAMtastic panel, the layer and aperture tables, Query and Measure, drill, aperture and status reports; objects erased and the layers exported again. File › Fabrication Outputs opens what it writes in a CAM document, as AD does.
items.alt: The CAM editor with the showcase board's Gerber and drill files

items.text: EAGLE: the Import Wizard (and File › Open) reads EAGLE 6 and later and Fusion Electronics' EAGLE schematics, boards and libraries; a schematic and a board of one name become one project. The Export Wizard writes the project as EAGLE 9's schematic, board and library.
items.alt: The Export Wizard on EAGLE with the showcase board behind it

items.text: Database libraries (.DbLib, .SVNDbLib) open, are made and are saved as AD writes them, on Excel workbooks, CSV, Access and SQLite databases. The Libraries panel lists their records as parts and places them as AD does; the demo project has one.
File › Save As saves schematics and boards in AD's ASCII formats too. Browsers without WebGL 2 (many older Windows computers) open documents again, drawn with the 2D canvas.

Fixed: 3D Layout Mode draws TrueType text on the overlay; File › Open (Ctrl+O) works in Chrome and Edge again; an auto-hide panel can be resized by the edge of its slide-out; the Preferences gear looks like a gear.

releases.title: OrCAD and Allegro export, ASCII PCB files

items.text: OrCAD and Allegro: File › Export Wizard › OrCAD and Allegro (AD ASCII Files), also File › Export › OrCAD and Allegro, writes the project in AD's own ASCII formats, which Cadence's translators for AD designs read (OrCAD Capture and PCB Editor 17.2 and later, File › Import): the project file and its structure file (the sheet tree), every schematic as an ASCII schematic and the board as an ASCII PCB file. Capture makes its parts from the schematics, PCB Editor its footprints from the board.
items.alt: The Export Wizard on OrCAD and Allegro with the showcase board behind it

items.text: ASCII PCB files: a .PcbDoc saved as PCB ASCII File (by AD, or by another tool's export to AD) opens as a board and is saved in ASCII again. ASCII schematics were already read and written.

Home page: What's New now sits in the middle column, so Get Konium Designer, Support Konium Designer and Report a bug stay in view. A copy opened from disk hears of new versions from konium.app again, and shows What's New. Texts an importer puts on a mechanical layer past 16 keep their layer.

releases.title: Import and export: KiCad, PADS, EasyEDA, OrCAD, Allegro, STL

items.text: File › Import Wizard (also File › Open, and dropping files or a folder on the window) brings other tools' designs in as AD projects: KiCad 6 and later (projects, schematics, boards, symbol and footprint libraries), PADS Logic and PADS Layout ASCII files, EasyEDA Standard and Pro (projects, backups and libraries), OrCAD Capture designs and libraries (.dsn, .olb, 16.0 and later), Allegro and OrCAD PCB Editor boards (.brd, 16.0 to 19) and IPC-2581 boards from any tool. A schematic and its board become one project with its nets named as the schematic compiles them, so Design › Update PCB has little or nothing to change; each tool's symbols and footprints come in as a SchLib and a PcbLib.
items.alt: The Import Wizard with the showcase project as KiCad files

items.text: What comes in: each sheet as a SchDoc with its parts as the tool places them, wires, buses, junctions, power ports, ports, off-sheet connectors, sheet symbols, title blocks and fonts; each board with its layer stack, outline and cut-outs, pads by their stacks (slots, custom shapes, mask and paste), tracks, arcs, vias (blind and buried), pours with their poured copper, keep-outs, text and drawings on named mechanical layers, and the design rules' clearances, widths and net classes. Where the other tool joins names that AD would not, the labels or connectors AD needs are added.

File › Export Wizard (also Export to another tool on the Home page): a project as KiCad 8 files (the project, schematics, board, symbol and footprint libraries with their tables, 3D models), as PADS ASCII files (PADS Logic and PADS Layout) or as EasyEDA Standard source files, into a folder or as a zip. Nets are written as the project compiles them and a multi-channel sheet once for each channel. Exported and imported again, the demo, the showcase and the real projects tried keep every net.
items.alt: The Export Wizard with the showcase project, KiCad Project chosen

items.text: STL: File › Export › STL 3D writes the board, drilled, with its bodies and models as one mesh, for printing or an enclosure's design. STL files open in the 3D model editor (saved as STEP), import there as parts and embed as a 3D body's model. STEP export now takes linked models too, not only embedded ones.
items.alt: The showcase board exported as STL and opened in the 3D model editor

items.text: Outputs: internal planes now plot in Gerber, Gerber X2, IPC-2581 and ODB++ as their copper, with their clearances and thermal reliefs (they were left out), worked out about three times faster; plane and polygon connect styles set per kind of object (pads, through-hole and SMD pads, vias) are used. TrueType PCB text plots at its true size.

Fixes: dotted, dashed and dash-dotted schematic lines were drawn solid (reported). Compile compared ports and sheet entries across sheets in the Connection Matrix, so hierarchical designs reported an Output Pin against another sheet's Input Port. Buses on sheet entries, ports and off-sheet connectors now join member by member as AD joins them, and a sheet symbol may name several files. DRC and connectivity are much faster on boards with large pours. What's New is at the top of the Home page's side column.

releases.title: Initial Release

items.text: Konium Designer is an electronics design tool for schematics, PCB layout, 3D and manufacturing outputs that runs in the browser, and offline once loaded. It opens, edits and saves AD's file formats (projects, schematics, boards, libraries, Output Jobs) and works as AD does: its menus, shortcuts, toolbars, dialogs and docking panels. The six-layer board in these pictures was designed, placed and routed in Konium Designer.
items.alt: A six-layer controller board in 3D, its schematic and a folded rigid-flex board

items.text: Schematic capture: multi-sheet and hierarchical designs with sheet symbols, ports, harnesses, buses, power ports and directives; every drawing and placing tool, Move and Drag that keep wires attached, the SCH Inspector, Filter and List; Compile with AD's error reporting and connection matrix; annotation, variants, the Parameter Manager and Update From Libraries; schematic libraries with multi-part symbols; Bill of Materials to Excel, CSV and HTML.
items.alt: The MCU and FPGA sheets of the showcase project and its Bill of Materials

items.text: PCB layout: interactive routing (Walkaround, Push, Hug And Push), differential pairs, bus routing, length tuning, dragging and via pushing; the autorouter and fanout; polygon pours, internal and split planes, teardrops, via stitching and shielding; design rules with online and batch DRC; the Layer Stack Manager with impedance; classes, rooms, unions, queries, the PCB panel, Filter and Inspector; Update PCB and Back Annotate, both ways.
items.alt: The routed six-layer board, its BGA fan-out and the Layer Stack Manager

items.text: 3D Layout Mode: the board at its layer stack's thickness with copper, mask, silkscreen and plated holes, every 3D body and its embedded or linked STEP model, and View Configurations as AD's. Rigid-flex: split and bending lines, a layer stack for each region, flex regions showing their polyimide where the stack has no mask, and Fold/Unfold (5) in 3D.
items.alt: The board in 3D close up, a rigid-flex board folded and in Board Planning Mode

items.text: Libraries and outputs: PCB libraries with the IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard (14 package families) and the component wizards, schematic and integrated libraries, library packages, and a 3D model editor for STEP files (move, turn, recolour, add boxes and cylinders, place on a footprint). Gerber RS-274X and X2, NC Drill, pick and place, STEP export, Draftsman fabrication and assembly drawings, print and PDF, and Output Jobs that make them all.
items.alt: The board exported to STEP in the 3D model editor, an IPC footprint in 3D and a Draftsman drawing
